caption: Figure. Schematic sequence of hepatitis B markers in acute infection that resolves. HBsAg clears before anti-HBs appears; in the window between them IgM anti-HBc is the only positive marker. Timings are illustrative.

Figure. Typical segment involvement in Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis. Crohn disease skips segments and often spares the rectum; ulcerative colitis always involves the rectum and extends proximally without gaps.

Figure. Two main molecular routes to colorectal cancer. Conventional adenomas progress through APC, KRAS and TP53 changes; sessile serrated lesions start with BRAF mutation and progress through CpG island methylation that silences MLH1.
Figure. Two molecular routes to colorectal cancer: the chromosomal instability pathway (APC, KRAS, TP53) and the serrated pathway (BRAF, CpG island methylation, MLH1 silencing).

Figure. Hepatocellular carcinoma surveillance in cirrhosis: nodule size on ultrasound decides between repeat ultrasound and multiphase imaging, and typical imaging features establish the diagnosis without biopsy.

Figure. The three routes of spread of gastrointestinal carcinoma: lymphatic to the thoracic duct and left supraclavicular node, hematogenous through the portal vein to the liver, and transcoelomic across the peritoneum to the omentum, pelvis and ovaries.

Figure. Approach to new ascites in a patient with cancer: the serum-ascites albumin gradient and cytology separate peritoneal carcinomatosis from portal hypertension caused by liver metastases, which guides palliation.
Figure. The four main inputs to the medullary vomiting centre, the receptors each uses, and the antiemetic classes that block them with their characteristic adverse effects.
Figure. A practical sort of white and red oral lesions by whether they wipe off, where they sit and their colour, with the malignant potential and next step for each.
Figure. Sorting dysphagia by history: oropharyngeal versus esophageal, then solids only (mechanical) versus solids and liquids (motility), and progressive versus intermittent course.
Figure. Three stimuli (histamine, gastrin, acetylcholine) and two inhibitors (somatostatin, prostaglandin E2) regulate the parietal cell proton pump; drug targets are labelled at each step.

Figure. Arterial territories of the colon: the splenic flexure lies between SMA and IMA supply and the rectosigmoid junction between IMA and internal iliac supply, the two segments most vulnerable to low-flow ischemia.
Figure. Management of CT-confirmed diverticulitis by severity, from selective antibiotics for uncomplicated disease to drainage or surgery for complicated disease, with colonoscopy after recovery.

Figure. The pectinate line separates endoderm-derived glandular mucosa with visceral innervation and portal venous drainage from ectoderm-derived squamous anoderm with somatic innervation, systemic venous drainage and inguinal lymph drainage.
Figure. Bilirubin moves from heme to unconjugated bilirubin, hepatocyte uptake, UGT1A1 conjugation and MRP2 export into bile; each hereditary hyperbilirubinemia blocks one of these steps.
Figure. The biliary tree and where a gallstone lodges for each classic complication; the level of obstruction predicts the clinical and laboratory picture.
Figure. Risk-based approach to a suspected common bile duct stone: high likelihood goes straight to ERCP, intermediate likelihood is confirmed with MRCP or endoscopic ultrasound first.
Figure. Pancreatic collections classified by whether the pancreatitis is necrotizing and by time since onset; only the later, walled forms are drained, and only when symptomatic or infected.

Figure. Classifying ascites: the serum-ascites albumin gradient separates portal hypertension from peritoneal causes, and ascitic total protein then separates cirrhosis from cardiac and hepatic vein causes.

Figure. Schematic of the groin viewed from inside. Direct hernias pass through Hesselbach triangle medial to the inferior epigastric vessels; indirect hernias enter the deep ring lateral to them; femoral hernias pass below the inguinal ligament medial to the femoral vein.
Figure. Simplified approach to blunt abdominal trauma: unstable patients get FAST and go to laparotomy if positive; stable patients get CT, and most solid organ injuries are managed without surgery.
Figure. The three divisions of the primitive gut, their arteries, main derivatives and the region where visceral pain is felt, with the timing of midgut herniation and rotation.

Figure. Acetaminophen metabolism. Most of the drug is conjugated; a minor CYP2E1 route forms NAPQI, which is safe while glutathione lasts and causes zone 3 necrosis once it is depleted. N-acetylcysteine restores glutathione.
